Public float, creations and redemptions

How much of an xStock's supply the public actually holds, and how many tokenized shares each issuer created and redeemed on Solana each day: like ETF flows, but read off the chain. Every figure comes from a transaction or account we read, with the time we read it. A day we did not read is shown as missing, never as zero; a day we read partly says how many hours; where a transaction shows no dollar amount the chart counts transactions instead, and a dollar total with units nothing could price is marked as a lower bound.

xStocks: public float is smaller than supply

Redeemed xStocks are not burned. The Base Prospectus defines de-activation as a transfer back to the wallet the Tokenizer holds for the Issuer, so redeemed tokens sit in issuer inventory and still count in the on-chain supply. Public float = mint supply − balances of the issuer-attributed wallets, read in raw units in one pass. Since 24 Sep 2026 those wallets include an inventory wallet that the issuer itself excludes from its circulating figure.
